Fallback Strategy: Fundamental baseline; no lower fallback
Deterministic Implications: Deterministic rasterization subject to CPU software floating-point implementations
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Direct retro pixel blitting, debug HUD rendering, auto-tiler preview rendering, and UI composition.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to DOM-bound <canvas> on main thread
Deterministic Implications: Deterministic rendering commands; transfer timing depends on browser compositor
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Decoupled render thread execution inside a Dedicated Web Worker to eliminate main-thread compositing stalls.

Fallback Strategy: Graceful degradation to Canvas 2D software blitter
Deterministic Implications: Minor shader floating-point precision divergence across heterogeneous GPU drivers
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Hardware-accelerated 2.5D raycasting wall extrusion, dynamic normal-mapped 2D lighting, and full-screen post-processing shaders.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to WebGL 2.0 pipeline; if unavailable, degrade to Canvas 2D
Deterministic Implications: High internal determinism; pipeline creation is immutable; floating-point ALU behavior conforms to WGSL specs
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Clustered forward lighting, modern deferred shading passes, and compute-based mesh skinning for 3D/pseudo-3D scenes.

Fallback Strategy: Degrade to WebAssembly SIMD or Web Worker CPU thread pool
Deterministic Implications: Deterministic across uniform workgroups; atomic contention resolution is order-dependent
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Mass GPU particle simulation (100,000+ embers/sparks), spatial hash grid construction, and real-time ray-traced shadow maps.

Fallback Strategy: Degrade to synchronous frame-slice execution on Main Thread
Deterministic Implications: Non-deterministic message dispatch timing across thread boundaries
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Dedicated thread host for the 60Hz fixed-timestep physics loop, spatial culling, and navigation mesh A* pathfinding.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to structured cloning (postMessage) with transferable ArrayBuffer
Deterministic Implications: High risk of race-driven non-determinism if synchronization primitives are misaligned; strictly deterministic via atomic read/writes
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Zero-copy linear memory sharing between Worker simulation and Main presentation threads for interpolated rendering.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to pure ECMAScript 2026 TypedArray arithmetic modules
Deterministic Implications: Strict IEEE-754 deterministic math execution across identical engine architectures
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Hot execution loops for continuous collision detection (CCD), ray-box intersections, and procedural level generation.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to scalar WebAssembly functions or scalar JavaScript loops
Deterministic Implications: Highly deterministic; hardware-accelerated 128-bit vector operations
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: 4-way parallel float32 vector mathematics, transformation matrix batching, and spatial bounding box culling.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to custom Atomic spinlocks within SharedArrayBuffer
Deterministic Implications: Non-deterministic lock acquisition ordering under heavy multi-tab contention
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Coordinating multi-tab state, master-tab election for engine telemetry, and preventing concurrent OPFS read/write corruption.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to asynchronous OPFS streams, IndexedDB, or LocalStorage
Deterministic Implications: Deterministic data persistence; asynchronous initiation introduces non-deterministic frame landing
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: High-speed, in-place binary reads and writes for engine world saves, SQLite database chunks, and persistent memory dumps.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to localStorage (limited to 5MB serialized strings)
Deterministic Implications: Non-deterministic asynchronous event completion timing
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Storage of serialized level maps, player profiles, cached audio blobs, and key-value game configuration data.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to hidden <input type="file"> DOM trigger
Deterministic Implications: Non-deterministic; strictly driven by asynchronous human interaction and OS file pickers
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Hot-reloading custom user mods, importing external sprite sheets, and direct disk export of world editor JSON/binary saves.

Fallback Strategy: Memory-only session caching via JavaScript Map<string, ArrayBuffer>
Deterministic Implications: Non-deterministic fetch arrival order; deterministic byte storage once cached
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Offline PWA assets, zero-latency caching of static runtime packages, audio buffers, and bundled sprite sheets.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to silent execution mode (null audio adapter)
Deterministic Implications: Hardware clock (ctx.currentTime) is deterministic; mixing buffer schedules depend on OS audio hardware sample rates
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Environmental audio graphs: dynamic multi-bus volume mixing, low-pass filter occlusion, and HRTF 3D spatial panning.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to pre-rendered HTML5 <audio> elements or synthetic Web Audio oscillator banks
Deterministic Implications: Sample-accurate, strictly deterministic DSP execution per 128-sample processing quantum
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Procedural sound synthesis (retro chip-tune synths, dynamic noise generation for explosions/wind, footstep generators) with zero GC latency.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to standard <video> / <audio> DOM element decoders
Deterministic Implications: Hardware-dependent frame decoding latency (non-deterministic decode frame arrival)
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Demuxing cutscenes, dynamic streaming of animated texture atlas video files directly to WebGL/WebGPU textures without DOM overhead.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to standard Keyboard and Mouse input mappings
Deterministic Implications: Polling is tied to frame invocations; timestamps depend on OS controller sampling rate
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Real-time analog stick navigation, trigger pressure reading, and physical haptic dual-rumble actuation feedback.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to standard clamped mouse drag tracking with visible cursor
Deterministic Implications: Mouse delta coordinates (movementX, movementY) are non-deterministic, hardware-bound inputs
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Unbounded first-person / third-person 3D camera rotation, precision crosshair aiming, and mouse-look navigation without desktop escapes.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to KeyboardEvent.key (subject to OS localization errors)
Deterministic Implications: Input timing is asynchronous and non-deterministic; buffered into deterministic ticks
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Layout-independent physical key binding (WASD / Space / Modifiers) mapped directly into atomic bitmasks.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to Date.now() (coarse millisecond resolution, vulnerable to OS clock changes)
Deterministic Implications: Monotonic microsecond clock; clock drift is mitigated via fixed-timestep accumulation
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Primary clock driving the fixed-step simulation accumulator, render delta time calculation, and micro-profiling benchmarks.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to WebSockets; fallback to HTTP long-polling if WebSockets blocked
Deterministic Implications: Highly non-deterministic packet arrival and packet loss characteristics
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Authoritative client-server synchronization using unreliable UDP-like datagrams for transforms and reliable streams for RPC commands.

Fallback Strategy: Fallback to client-server WebSockets relay server
Deterministic Implications: Unreliable/unordered network delivery creates non-deterministic packet arrivals
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Zero-server peer-to-peer multiplayer state exchange, direct voice/data transmission, and decentralized cooperative sessions.

Fallback Strategy: Direct network loading without offline pre-caching
Deterministic Implications: Non-deterministic cache hit/miss resolution during initial boot sequence
Concrete Emberlight Use Case: Intercepting network requests, guaranteeing complete offline capability for single-file engine installations, and handling PWA updates.
